description: A composite figure of two parts: a strength-contribution table and a dual-axis mechanical-property plot. The table lists rolling states HR45, HR68 and HR82 against sigma_0, sigma_p-kappa, sigma_p-(Nb,Mo,W)C, sigma_ds, sigma_gb, sigma_calc and sigma_exp (all in MPa): sigma_0 is constant at 203.1 MPa; sigma_p-kappa = 61.0/58.0/60.2; sigma_p-(Nb,Mo,W)C = 6.5/6.7/6.4; sigma_ds = 56.3/93.7/107.5; sigma_gb = 157.0/215.8/276.8; sigma_calc = 483.9/577.3/653.9 and sigma_exp = 480.0/577.0/648.0 MPa, so calculated and experimentally tested yield strengths agree closely. The plot (Fig. 10) has true strain epsilon_t (0-0.40) on x, true stress sigma_t (MPa, 0-4000) on the left y and strain-hardening rate dsigma/depsilon (MPa) on the right y. Solid lines are sigma_t-epsilon_t curves (grey HR45, red HR68, blue HR82) rising to roughly 1300 MPa; dashed lines are the corresponding (dsigma/depsilon)-epsilon_t curves, which fall steeply after yielding and then hold near 2000 MPa. Stage I / Stage II / Stage III brackets are drawn for each sample, and three arrows mark the interrupted tensile tests at epsilon_c = 0.1, 0.2 and 0.4.

observations.observation: The table reports the same sigma_0 = 203.1 MPa for all three rolling states HR45, HR68 and HR82.
sigma_gb rises from 157.0 MPa (HR45) to 215.8 MPa (HR68) to 276.8 MPa (HR82) with increasing hot-rolling reduction.
sigma_ds increases from 56.3 MPa (HR45) to 93.7 MPa (HR68) to 107.5 MPa (HR82), the largest relative change of any term.
Calculated yield strengths sigma_calc (483.9, 577.3, 653.9 MPa) closely match the experimentally tested sigma_exp (480.0, 577.0, 648.0 MPa) for HR45, HR68 and HR82.

In the plot the grey solid curve is labelled HR45, the red solid curve HR68 and the blue solid curve HR82 for sigma_t-epsilon_t, with matching dashed (dsigma/depsilon)-epsilon_t curves of the same three samples.
The solid true stress-strain curves rise continuously over the whole 0-0.40 strain range, with blue HR82 highest and grey HR45 lowest, reaching roughly the 1300 MPa level at 0.40 strain.
The dashed strain-hardening-rate curves drop steeply immediately after yielding and then remain at a high level near 2000 MPa before decreasing continuously to the end of the plot.
Three vertical arrows labelled epsilon_c = 0.1, epsilon_c = 0.2 and epsilon_c = 0.4 are drawn on the plot at increasing true strains.
The caption states the arrows indicate at which strains the tensile tests were interrupted.
The caption states the figure summarises the strengthening contribution of different mechanisms to the yield strength together with the experimentally tested results of the investigated samples.

Stage I, Stage II and Stage III brackets are annotated separately for each of the three samples, covering the initial drop after yielding, the gradual increase to peak values and the continuous decrease until fracture.

The citing text states the three-staged strain-hardening behaviour keeps the strain-hardening rate at a high level of ~2000 MPa over a wide range of plastic strain, contributing to the excellent ductility.
The citing text states that the strain-hardening rates of the present steel increased continuously with increasing hot-rolling reduction.
The citing text states the steel has a high stacking fault energy of ~73 mJ/m2, which the text notes makes its strain-hardening evolution different from conventional high-SFE fcc metals.

subfigures.description: Eight-column table of rolling states HR45, HR68, HR82 with strengthening contributions in MPa: sigma_0 (203.1 for all), sigma_p-kappa (61.0/58.0/60.2), sigma_p-(Nb,Mo,W)C (6.5/6.7/6.4), sigma_ds (56.3/93.7/107.5), sigma_gb (157.0/215.8/276.8), sigma_calc (483.9/577.3/653.9) and sigma_exp (480.0/577.0/648.0).

Dual-axis plot: true stress sigma_t (MPa, left axis 0-4000) and strain-hardening rate dsigma/depsilon (MPa, right axis) versus true strain epsilon_t (0-0.40). Three solid sigma_t-epsilon_t curves (HR45 grey, HR68 red, HR82 blue) and three dashed (dsigma/depsilon)-epsilon_t curves of the same samples; Stage I-III brackets and arrows labelled epsilon_c = 0.1, 0.2, 0.4.

unreadable_items: The caption text rendered inside the upper-left of the plot overlaps the dashed strain-hardening-rate curves, so the exact starting dsigma/depsilon values at the lowest strains cannot be read
The exact x-axis positions of the epsilon_c = 0.1, 0.2 and 0.4 arrows are known only from their printed labels, not from the plotted curves themselves
Right-hand y-axis tick labels for dsigma/depsilon are partially obscured by the overlying legend/caption text
